title: Nscale owns the power and the data centres. For ~$1.65bn, it just bought the software too.
excerpt: Nscale, the London AI-cloud company that owns its own power and data centres, is buying its way up the stack. It has agreed to acquire Anyscale, the startup behind the widely used Ray software. Bloomberg reported the deal at about $1.65bn. Nscale announced the acquisition on Thursday but did not put a price on it. […]
content_html:
Nscale, the London AI-cloud company that owns its own power and data centres, is buying its way up the stack. It has agreed to acquire Anyscale, the startup behind the widely used Ray software. Bloomberg reported the deal at about $1.65bn.

Nscale announced the acquisition on Thursday but did not put a price on it. Bloomberg gave the figure, citing a person familiar with the deal. Anyscale’s 200 or so staff, spread across the US, Europe and India, will join Nscale. The deal should close in the second half of 2026.

Why a power company buys software

Nscale’s pitch has always been that it owns the layers beneath the chip: the electricity, the buildings, the racks. Buying Anyscale moves it up into the software that decides how much useful work each expensive GPU actually does.

The logic is about margins. Renting raw GPUs by the hour is a commodity business, fought against every rival buying the same Nvidia systems. The money sits a layer up, in how a job gets split across thousands of chips at once.

Anyscale’s platform, built on the open-source Ray framework, does exactly that. It spreads data preparation, training, fine-tuning and inference across a whole fleet. The company claims that cuts total cost of ownership by up to 90% against a patchwork of separate tools.

“Most infrastructure providers just buy GPUs and rent them,” said Josh Payne, Nscale’s chief executive and founder. He said Nscale instead builds and owns every layer itself: the power, the data centres, the compute and the software.

Its product chief, Dan Bathurst, put the pitch plainly. An engineer can now come to Nscale, he said, as “a one-stop shop for all of their training, fine-tuning and inference services.”

The neocloud land grab

Nscale is one of the “neoclouds,” the wave of AI-focused data-centre newcomers chasing the boom. It grew out of a cryptocurrency-mining business in early 2024. It has moved fast since, passing 1GW of capacity and signing big compute deals.

It has also lined up the money to keep building. In July it closed a $900m revolving credit facility, on top of a $2.5bn commitment to UK data centres. It plans to float, possibly later this year. Its board includes the former Meta executives Sheryl Sandberg and Nick Clegg.

Its rivals are making the same move. In May, Nebius spent $643m to buy Eigen AI, another firm that makes AI run more cheaply. The chipmaker Qualcomm bought the compiler startup Modular this month. “Everyone’s wanting to move up the stack,” Bathurst told Bloomberg. The prize is to be the one-stop shop as the money floods into AI infrastructure.

What Nscale is actually buying

The open-source project at the centre of the deal is not for sale. The PyTorch Foundation took over Ray in 2025, and it had already logged some 237 million downloads. It stays community-governed and free to run anywhere, from Cursor to xAI.

Nscale is buying the commercial platform, the engineering team and the customers, which include Coinbase, Runway and Bedrock Robotics. Anyscale was founded in 2019 by the Berkeley researchers who built Ray. They are Robert Nishihara, Philipp Moritz and Ion Stoica, who also co-founded Databricks. Nscale will join the foundation too.

Anyscale arrives with momentum, reporting 70% revenue growth in its most recent quarter. Its chief executive, Keerti Melkote, called the combined company “the first full-stack AI hyperscaler.” That is the bet: own everything from the electricity to the trained model. It is the same logic behind the race to build national AI factories.

Whether it pays off is a question of timing. Anyscale sells against capacity that runs today. Nscale’s largest deployment, a 1.35GW site for Microsoft in West Virginia, only starts arriving in 2027.

content_html_zh:
Nscale 是一家伦敦人工智能云公司，拥有自己的电力和数据中心，正在通过收购来提升自己的地位。 它已同意收购 Anyscale，这是广泛使用的 Ray 软件背后的初创公司。 彭博社报道称，这笔交易金额约为 16.5 亿美元。

Nscale 周四宣布了此次收购，但没有给出具体价格。 彭博社援引一位知情人士的话给出了这一数字。 Anyscale 分布在美国、欧洲和印度的 200 名左右员工将加入 Nscale。 该交易预计将于 2026 年下半年完成。

电力公司为何购买软件

Nscale 的宣传一直是它拥有芯片下面的各个层：电力、建筑物、机架。 购买 Anyscale 将其提升到软件中，该软件决定每个昂贵的 GPU 实际做了多少有用的工作。

逻辑是关于利润的。 按小时租用原始 GPU 是一项商品业务，与购买相同 Nvidia 系统的所有竞争对手相抗衡。 这笔钱位于更高的一层，即一项工作如何同时分配到数千个芯片上。

Anyscale 的平台基于开源 Ray 框架构建，正是这样做的。 它将数据准备、训练、微调和推理扩展到整个机队。 该公司声称，与拼凑不同的工具相比，总拥有成本可降低高达 90%。

Nscale 首席执行官兼创始人 Josh Payne 表示：“大多数基础设施提供商只是购买 GPU 并租用它们。” 他表示，Nscale 自行构建并拥有每一层：电力、数据中心、计算和软件。

其产品负责人丹·巴瑟斯特 (Dan Bathurst) 的表述很直白。 他说，工程师现在可以来到 Nscale，作为“所有培训、微调和推理服务的一站式商店”。

Neocloud 的抢地盘

Nscale 是“neoclouds”之一，这是一波追逐繁荣的专注于人工智能的数据中心新来者浪潮。 它起源于 2024 年初的加密货币挖矿业务。 此后，它的发展速度很快，容量已超过 1GW，并签署了大型计算交易。

它还准备了资金来继续建设。 7 月，除了向英国数据中心承诺 25 亿美元之外，它还关闭了一项 9 亿美元的循环信贷安排。 它计划上市，可能在今年晚些时候。 其董事会成员包括前 Meta 高管谢丽尔·桑德伯格 (Sheryl Sandberg) 和尼克·克莱格 (Nick Clegg)。

它的竞争对手也在采取同样的举措。 今年 5 月，Nebius 斥资 6.43 亿美元收购了 Eigen AI，这是另一家让人工智能运行成本更低的公司。 芯片制造商高通本月收购了编译器初创公司 Modular。 “每个人都想晋升，”巴瑟斯特告诉彭博社。 随着资金涌入人工智能基础设施，我们的目标是成为一站式商店。

Nscale 实际购买的是什么

交易核心的开源项目不出售。 PyTorch 基金会于 2025 年接管 Ray，下载量已达到约 2.37 亿次。 它仍然由社区管理，并且可以在从 Cursor 到 xAI 的任何地方自由运行。

Nscale 正在收购商业平台、工程团队和客户，其中包括 Coinbase、Runway 和 Bedrock Robotics。 Anyscale 由构建 Ray 的伯克利研究人员于 2019 年创立。 他们是 Robert Nishihara、Philipp Moritz 和 Ion Stoica，他们也是 Databricks 的联合创始人。 Nscale 也将加入该基金会。

Anyscale 势头强劲，最近一个季度的收入增长了 70%。 其首席执行官 Keerti Melkote 将合并后的公司称为“第一家全栈人工智能超大规模企业”。 这就是赌注：拥有从电力到训练模型的一切。 国家人工智能工厂竞相建设也是同样的逻辑。

是否有回报只是时间问题。 Anyscale 根据当前运行的容量进行销售。 Nscale 最大的部署是微软位于西弗吉尼亚州的 1.35GW 站点，该站点将于 2027 年开始抵达。
